speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle and now increasing pain and swelling in your right knee along with episodes of painful urination. To understand the connection between these symptoms, have you noticed any fever, fatigue, or skin rashes recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome).

The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (ankle then knee), urethritis (painful urination), and recent sexual activity in a young male is highly suggestive of this condition. Given the 12-day duration and current knee swelling, I request an image of the right knee. REQUEST IMAGES
